title: A case-insensitive tag set
description:
Write `final class Tag implements Comparable<Tag>` for labels such as `"Java"` or `"java"` that should count as the **same** tag:

- `Tag.of(String text)` trims the text; blank text throws `IllegalArgumentException`. It keeps the text as given (after trimming) for display.
- `equals` and `hashCode` ignore case (compare with `toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)`).
- `compareTo` orders alphabetically ignoring case, and is **consistent with equals** (0 exactly when equal).
- `toString()` returns the text as given.

Then write `class Tags` with `static Set<Tag> distinct(List<String> raw)` returning the distinct tags sorted (a `TreeSet`), keeping the **first** spelling seen of each.

```java
Tags.distinct(List.of("Java", "rust", " JAVA ", "Go", "java")).toString();   // [Go, Java, rust]
```
hints: Work out the lower-case key once in the constructor and use it in `equals`, `hashCode` and `compareTo`: that keeps all three consistent by construction.
`Set.add` does nothing when an equal element is already there, so the first spelling wins without any extra code.
lessonTitle: equals, hashCode and the Object Contract
